item.title: The daily tape · 1 September 2026
item.description: Texas cleared real steel on Friday: PUCT unanimously approved Oncor’s ~424-mile / ~$3.95B 765-kV Import Path 1 (59315 Route 559 + 59029 Route 476), while Howard–Solstice (59336) is still stuck past the 31 Aug statutory clock. Reuters’ Sep 1 ghost-demand frame puts TX interconnection requests near 474 GW against a peak an order of magnitude smaller — conversion is now gated by which CCNs close and which audits kill paper load. Silicon Tape: confirm day — Lambda H100 $3.99 / B200 $6.69, 62 confirms, 0 ticks; first history prints for GCP TPU v5e OD/1y/3y ($1.20 / $0.84 / $0.54). Countries: United States: PUCT, 28 Aug: unanimous final CCNs for Oncor Import Path 1 — Dinosaur–Longshore (59315 Route 559, ~242.6 mi, ~$2.243B, target 2028) and Longshore–Drill Hole (59029 Route 476, ~181.6 mi, ~$1.704B, target 2029); ~424 miles / ~$3.95B of 765-kV under the Permian Basin Reliability Plan. Need findings cited oil/gas plus non-oil load (crypto, data centers, hydrogen). Wire today. Source: Dallas Express / Oncor / Texas Tribune. United States: Late Aug reporting (Forbes 31 Aug; TechTimes 29 Aug citing The Information): Commerce/BIS drafting a remote-access export-control rule to treat rental of advanced AI GPUs as controlled access, aimed at Chinese firms via third-country DCs (Thailand, Singapore). House already passed H.R. 2683 (RASA); Senate has not. Draft text unpublished — Policy/Stall conversion on usable FLOPs geography. Wire today. Source: Forbes / Congress.gov. Taiwan: Powertech Technology, 27 Aug: FOPLP AI packaging capacity fully booked through 2030 by two majors (press: AMD, Broadcom); ~NT$70B (~$2.2B) ramp from ~1,000 to ~5,000 panels/month by 2028; AI server CPU shipments next year; Broadcom joint line planned in Singapore ~2028. Packaging-conversion print around CoWoS scarcity. Wire today. Source: Taipei Times / Nikkei Asia. United States: Reuters, 1 Sep: Texas interconnection requests near ~474 GW versus a peak load an order of magnitude smaller — the “ghost demand” frame. Conversion now hinges on which CCNs close and which ERCOT/utility audits kill paper load. Brief only; not a new Wire id. Source: Reuters. United States: Howard–Solstice (PUCT Docket 59336) remains tabled past the 31 Aug statutory CCN clock. No Interchange final order located. HOLD Wire. Source: Texas Tribune / PUCT Interchange. United States: Georgia Power, 26 Aug: 3,200 MW OpenAI Effingham contract on the PSC staff path; OpenAI pays full infrastructure cost; up to 1,000 MW flexible DR. Public summary still due ~5 Sep. Source: Georgia Power / Southern Company. Australia: George Town Council, 25 Aug: 6–1 approval of Firmus 288 MW at Bell Bay. 14-day TASCAT appeal window runs into early September. Source: ABC News.
